title: reduce-streaming-token-latency-kernel-scheduling-kv-cache-batching-backpressure-flush-cadence
author: Samir Patel
description: Context: Streaming token generation latency has remained the dominant contributor to perceived latency in low-latency workloads (chat/interactive assistants). Previous mitigations (larger flush intervals, very small window batching) either increased tail latency under bursty traffic or caused higher cost due to poor batching/kernel utilization. Motivation: Reduce p50/p95 token emit latency without regressing throughput by combining focused kernel scheduling improvements, KV-cache prefetch/hinting, and an adaptive continuous-batching + flush cadence that cooperates with backpressure signals. Summary of changes: 1) Token loop: refactor to non-blocking emit paths, remove synchronous flush in hot path, introduce token-emit state machine that performs opportunistic user-facing flushes while leaving commit/background flush for durability. 2) Flush cadence: new adaptive flush scheduler that balances latency vs batch utilization based on recent inter-token intervals and active request concurrency. Default policy reduces flush window for interactive streams but expands slightly when many concurrent streams are present to improve kernel amortization. 3) Backpressure: dynamic backpressure thresholds and early-shed heuristics; when GPU queue depth is high, the scheduler increases batch window but prioritizes single-stream low-latency flushes via the kernel scheduler (see below). 4) Kernel scheduling: introduce small-batch prioritization queue and preemption window for short-context streams; scheduling weights prefer kernels with low setup overhead for 1-8 token batches to reduce p50 latency. 5) KV cache: add prefetch hints and lightweight cache-touching for streams with high token locality; enable fast-path cache lookup that avoids mutex contention in the hot path and falls back to existing lock when contention detected. 6) Continuous batching: windowed continuous batching now supports adaptive windows per-stream class (interactive vs bulk) and aligns batch boundaries to maximize KV cache hits and reduce kernel launches. Benchmarks: - Microbench (single small stream, 1-2 token tokens/sec bursts): p50 token emit latency reduced from 38ms to 18ms (-53%), p95 from 140ms to 62ms (-56%). - Multistream (50 concurrent interactive streams): p50 reduced 24%, p95 reduced 30% while maintaining throughput within 3% of baseline. - Throughput tests on large-batch workloads show <1% regression. Canary: Rolled out to perf-canary fleet for 48h on Dedicated capacity; observed stable CPU/GPU utilization and no regressions in memory. Migration and config: New config knobs (streaming.flush_policy, scheduling.small_batch_priority, kv.prefetch) with safe defaults. We expose an opt-in feature flag `streaming.low_latency_mode` for Dedicated customers; hosted default will be enabled for interactive model classes after canary. Testing: unit tests for token loop state machine, integration tests for adaptive flush scheduler under synthetic workloads, load tests in perf-canary. Rollout Plan: staged canary -> gradual rollout across regions with metrics gating (p50/p95 token latency, kernel launch rate, GPU queue depth). Checklist: - [x] Token loop refactor and unit tests - [x] Adaptive flush scheduler + tests - [x] Kernel scheduler changes and synthetic benchmarks - [x] KV cache fast-path + contention fallback - [x] CI and smoke tests - [x] Canary run and monitoring dashboards Notes: This PR intentionally keeps changes behind config flags and runtime feature toggles where appropriate to allow fast rollback. See linked Linear tasks for follow-ups on metric tuning and SDK compatibility. Related: ENG-2123 (low-latency streaming), ENG-2197 (kv-cache improvements).

review_comments: Jordan Lee: Nice end-to-end work. Two questions: 1) how do we ensure KV prefetch doesn't regress memory use? 2) Please add a short description of the token state machine transitions in the code comments.

Samir Patel (author): KV prefetch is bounded by per-stream soft limit and only enabled when cache hit rate > 65% in the last N tokens; added comments and state machine diagram to token_loop.rs. See commit d4e9c12 and a7b3c4d.
Maya Chen: Can we add a safety gate if kernel preemption causes thrashing under high concurrency? Suggest a simple token count-based cooldown.
Samir Patel (author): Added a cooldown heuristic and test to kernel_scheduler (commit f8923ea). Cooldown enabled only when preemption events > 5 in 10s window.
Evan Cruz: CI showed flaky test failure on the first canary run, re-ran CI and canary. Results look clean now. Approving.
Jordan Lee: Approved after verifying canary dashboards; p95 improvements look real and no memory regressions observed.
release_notes: Reduced streaming token emit latency by up to 50% p50 and ~55% p95 for low-latency interactive streams via kernel scheduling, KV-cache fast-paths, adaptive flush cadence, and backpressure-aware batching. Feature behind streaming.low_latency_mode flag.
notes: Follow-ups tracked in ENG-2248 (metric tuning) and ENG-2260 (SDK streaming compatibility tests). Rollout monitored via console dashboards: streaming.token_emit_latency.{p50,p95}, scheduling.kernel_launch_rate, kv.cache_hit_rate.
